name: IL-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Strongly Democratic district with an 18-point partisan lean
Incumbent Jonathan Jackson running for reelection with a large fundraising edge
Republican challenger Christian Maxwell has minimal resources and no outside support
Prediction markets price Jackson at about 95% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point overwhelmingly to Jackson: a deep-blue Chicago-area seat, incumbency, and a fundraising advantage of roughly seven to one over Maxwell, with no polling or ratings suggesting a competitive race. Markets agree, pricing Jackson near 95%, so only a modest trim from the fundamentals-based margin is warranted.
model.watch: Any late surge of outside spending against Jackson or an unexpectedly strong Republican turnout environment could narrow the margin, though an upset remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jonathan Jackson, the Democratic incumbent in this heavily Democratic Chicago district, is seeking reelection against Republican Christian Maxwell. The seat's partisan lean of roughly 18 points Democratic gives Jackson a substantial structural advantage, and he is running as an established incumbent with the benefits that come with it.

Fundraising shows a clear gap: Jackson has raised about $418,000 to Maxwell's roughly $63,000, and neither campaign reports meaningful outside spending. No public general-election polling is available, but prediction markets price Jackson's chances at about 95 percent. The combination of district lean, incumbency, and the money gap makes this a Safe Democratic race, with Maxwell needing an extraordinary shift to compete.
